Where the numbers come from

Prices come from the OSRS Wiki real-time price feed, which collects completed Grand Exchange trades from RuneLite users. Buy is the latest insta-sell price (what a buy offer at that price fills at). Sell is the latest insta-buy price. Trades/hr is the number of items traded in the last hour on both sides.

The tax

The GE takes 2% of the sell price on every completed sale, rounded down per item, capped at 5,000,000 gp per item. Items that sell for under 50 gp pay nothing because 2% rounds down to zero. A short list of items is exempt (bonds, basic tools, cheap food, teleport tablets, bronze to steel arrows and darts, energy potions, games necklaces, rings of dueling and mind runes). Every margin and profit figure on this page already has the tax removed.

Margin = Sell − Buy − min(floor(Sell × 0.02), 5,000,000)

Profit / 4h

Margin multiplied by how many you can realistically move in one buy-limit window (4 hours). That quantity is the smallest of three caps: the buy limit, what your cash stack covers, and your share of the hourly volume (the slower side of the last hour's trades × 4 × the share you set). The small text under each figure says which cap applied. The volume cap is what stops an item with a giant spread and three trades an hour from topping the list. Set it to "Ignore volume" to see pure buy-limit numbers.

Flags

  • Swing: the latest trade is more than 15% away from the hourly average on either side. Often a single odd trade or someone manipulating the price. Verify before committing.
  • Stale: the older of the two prices is past your max age. The margin may no longer exist.
  • Slow: fewer items trade per hour than a quarter of the buy limit, so filling the full limit will take a long time.
  • No tax: tax rounds to zero or the item is exempt.

Before you commit gold

Margin-check in game: buy one at the Sell price, then sell it at the Buy price. If the real margin matches, scale up. Hourly volume and age tell you whether a margin is real; a huge margin on an item that trades twice a day is usually not.

How to read this list

Each row is one way to make money. Profit / hr is what it pays after GE tax at the rate shown. Three kinds of figure:

  • LIVE: skilling, processing and collecting with fixed inputs and outputs, priced from the Grand Exchange feed right now. Do the actions at the rate shown and this is what you make.
  • ESTIMATE · DROP TABLE / ESTIMATE · REWARDS: PvM, chests, minigame rewards and anything else that depends on drops. The drop table is priced live, but the result is a long-run average; your hour will differ, and rare drops carry most of the value.
  • ESTIMATE · WIKI: the Wiki guide's own figure, used only where there is nothing to price (points rewards, raids) or where a drop table's rates depend on team size.
  • Per action is the profit for one kill, trip, cast or item. Rate is how many you do an hour. The guide's rate is the default; open a row to type your own, and it is remembered.
  • When the rate says capped, the key item doesn't trade fast enough to sell everything you'd make, so the rate is lowered to your share of the last hour's volume (Market cap, in the filters).
  • Cash / hr is the gold you put in each hour. Trades / hr is how often the key item changes hands; under 20 is thin, under 200 is slow.
  • Difficulty combines the highest level needed, every quest (longer and harder quests count more), click intensity, dangerous areas and extra unlocks. Hover or tap it for the breakdown.
  • Your levels: look up your name or type levels in, then tick Only show what I can do. For skilling, only the Wiki's hard requirement counts (a "90+ recommended" is advice). For PvM, the Wiki's recommended combat stats are treated as requirements, because they are what you need to actually kill the thing.
  • Open any row for the full working: supplies, outputs, every option for methods with several products, the drop table for monsters, requirements, where to go and a 7-day trend.
  • Instant prices buy supplies at insta-buy and sell at insta-sell. Patient is the reverse and shows the ceiling if your offers fill.

How alching is calculated

High Level Alchemy turns an item into 60% of its store value in coins; Low Level Alchemy gives 40%. The alch value never changes, so profit depends only on what you pay for the item and the runes.

Profit per cast = alch value − item price − nature rune − fire runes (unless you hold a fire staff)

  • Grand Exchange: every tradeable item with an alch value, priced from the live feed. Buy limits are per 4 hours, so the sustainable rate is limit ÷ 4 per hour, and the page caps your casts per hour at that for each item. Profit / 4h is one full buy-limit cycle (or what your cash stack covers).
  • Shops: every shop that sells an alchable item for coins, from the OSRS Wiki's store data. The price shown is at full stock; shops raise the price by their delta % for each one you buy and drop it back as stock returns (restock time is shown). Stock × shops across worlds is your real limit. The GE column shows what the item sells for if you'd rather flip it than alch it.
  • Casts per hour: 1,200 is the hard cap (one cast every 3 seconds). Enter your real rate if you alch while doing something else.
  • Items whose latest trade is more than 15% off the hourly average are hidden by default: one odd trade can make an alch look profitable for a minute.

How this works

Both of these happen entirely at the Grand Exchange, need no levels or quests, and are free and instant. The only skill is buying and selling, so every figure here is live.

  • Potion decanting: lower doses often sell for less than their share of a full potion. Buy them, right-click the GE clerk → Decant (or Bob Barter next to the clerk) and everything in your inventory combines into the highest dose. Profit = full-dose sell − tax − (doses needed × dose price). The source dose's trade volume and buy limit are the bottleneck, so those are what the row shows.
  • Item sets: right-click the GE clerk → Sets to pack pieces into one set item or unpack a set into its pieces. The row shows whichever direction pays; open it for both. Sets have their own 4-hour buy limit, so buying sets and unpacking them gets you more of a piece than its own limit allows. Sets themselves trade slowly: the Trades / hr column is the set's own volume (red under 5), and the min-trades filter applies to the pieces.
  • Profit / 4h is one buy-limit cycle at the tightest limit in the chain, or what your cash stack buys if that is smaller. Thin rows are marked in red (under 20 trades an hour for a potion dose, under 5 for a set): the margin is real but you may wait a long time to fill.
  • Rows whose item has not traded both ways in the last day are hidden along with price swings, because a day-old price is not a price you can get.
  • Prices are the hourly average from the Wiki feed with the latest trade as fallback, the same basis as the Alchemy tab. Rows with a price swing (latest trade more than 15% off the average) are hidden by default.
